steps.npc: Greetings, traveller.
Gah! A bunch of fanatical cultists. Nothing more.

steps.text: If the player has not yet defeated The Nightmare:

steps.npc: No! Well I wouldn't be, would I? I've spent my whole life dedicated to my sect. I dreamed of one day entering the Sanctuary and finally meeting Mother!
Yet instead I'm greeted by this condescending 'Lord' who feels I could try being 'a little more chaotic' for once.
And to top it all off, Mother hasn't awoken at all. I fear she is probably being held captive by this Nightmare, or worse.
The only things these oafs are breaking is my head with their silent stares and furious hand-talk.

steps.player: I'm sorry your day hasn't been going well.

steps.npc: Ah... Thank you, traveller. Are you here to fight the Nightmare?
I'll pray for you.

steps.text: If the player has previously defeated The Nightmare, there is a chance the following branch will be displayed:

steps.player: They seem to be carrying dangerous weapons.

steps.npc: Indeed. Speaking of weapons, I assume you have heard of the immensely powerful orbs the Nightmare is protecting?

steps.player: Yes I have. In fact, I've managed to beat the Nightmare myself.
Anyway, as you've heard of the orbs I assume you've also heard of the even stronger Bashyhammer of Ashihama?

steps.npc: The what?
But you just said...

steps.player: ...Trashyhammer of Ashihama. Yes, I know what I said.

steps.npc: Wha-
That doesn't even make sense.
Too far. I'm done.
These are the masks of the Sisterhood. While symbolic, they also have practical uses.
Herbs can be stored within the beak, masking the smell of death and preventing us from becoming infected.

steps.player: That sounds handy. Can I have one?

steps.npc: You ask too many questions.
It's a no. To wear a mask of the Sisterhood, you need to join the Sisterhood.
An ancient order, born right here in Slepe.
You lack the qualities we're currently looking for. Perhaps another time.

options.text: Tell me more about the Sisterhood.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Sisterhood.

steps.npc: Many years ago, the Sisterhood were a group of healers dedicated to Saradomin.
However, our leader, a justiciar known as Phosani, saw the truth in Saradomin's teachings and turned away from his false light.
Phosani embraced the glory of Zamorak and most of our order did the same. After that, she became known as the Inquisitor, though our order refers to her as 'Mother'.
After the order reached enlightenment through Zamorak, we made our home in an abandoned hermitage. Over time, that hermitage grew into the town you see today.

steps.player: What happened to those that refused to turn away from Saradomin?

steps.npc: They were shown the error of their ways through fire and blood.
Be safe, traveller.
